full_judgment: 3. The prosecution case, in brief, is that Meser Ali gifted. 58 decimal of land of Plot Nos. 1283 and 1241 of Khatian No. 1095 of Mouza Khetal to his daughters, namely, Rokeya Begum (PW 1), Sufi a Khatun (PW 2) and Momena Khatun by deed of Heba-bil-Ewaz (Ext. 1) dated 17-9-1974; accused Akkas Ali step-brother of the said donees and son of the donor created a forged deed in respect of  .99  decimal of land of Plot Nos. 1230 and 1241 including a portion of land already gifted by Meser Ali to his aforesaid daughters and got it registered in Bogra Sadar Registration Office on 25-3-1974. Accused Akkas Ali applied for agricultural loan to Joypurhat Agricultural Bank on the basis of the forged deed. During inquiry by the Bank the forgery became known to Meger Ali and his daughters. Then Meser Ali filed OC Suit No. 18 of 1977 in the Court of Munsif, Joypurhat for declaration that Heba-bil-Ewaz deed dated 25-3-1974 purporting to be executed and registered by him in favour of his son accused Akkas Ali is forged, illegal, null and void and not binding upon him. Meser Ali after filing of the suit died and his daughters substituted themselves in the place of Meser Ali and proceeded with the suit. The suit was decreed. Thereafter Rokeya filed a petition of complaint (Ext. 6) to the Court of SDM Bogra alleging forgery against accused Akkas Ali and Saidur Rahman. The SDM forwarded the petition of complaint to the DAB Bogra for inquiry and starting a case. Accordingly, at the inquiry alamats were seized and handwriting and thumb impressions were examined by Handwriting and Finger Print Experts. The thumb impressions of deceased Meser Ali appearing in the deed of gift executed and registered on 20-2-1970 differed from the thumb impressions appearing in Heba-bil-Ewaz dated 25-3-1974 and on receipt of the reports of experts, being satisfied that forgery was committed Md Shahjahan Ali, AI of DAB lodged the first information report as the informant. On completion of investigation charge sheet was submitted against the accused Akkas Ali Mollah and Saidur Rahman to face trial. Charges were framed against the accused under section 467 of the Penal Code to which they pleaded not guilty. The defence of the accused Akkas Ali is that his father Meser Ali made a deed of gift in his favour with full knowledge by the deed of gift dated 25-3-1974 and he committed no forgery. The defence of the accused Saidur Rahman is that he did not identity Meser Ali, the executant of the alleged forged deed, at the time of registration.
